input_box_content.user_input_content: === CHARACTER LOCK — STRICT === RIVEN: Use the provided Riven reference image as the strict primary character reference. Preserve Riven's exact facial identity, facial structure, pale-blonde hair, hairstyle, body proportions, clothing and armor design, sword design, overall silhouette, and grounded warrior appearance. Riven must remain unmistakably the same character throughout the entire video. This scene takes place many years after Riven's childhood, immediately before she leaves her home to join the army. Her original character design must remain unchanged. Do not redesign her costume. Do not change her hairstyle. Do not change her body proportions. Do not replace or redesign her sword. Riven is already a highly skilled swordswoman after many years of training. She is fast, confident, physically capable, and disciplined. Her movement must remain grounded and human. Riven has already made the private decision to leave home. She is not frightened by that decision. She is determined. FATHER: Use the provided Father reference image as the strict primary visual reference for Riven's father. Preserve his recognizable facial appearance, age, hairstyle, facial hair, body proportions, clothing design, and grounded former-warrior appearance. He is an experienced former warrior. His movements are economical, calm, precise, and controlled. He relies on timing, positioning, experience, and efficient footwork. He knows Riven extremely well. He already understands that Riven intends to leave home. He does not try to stop her. Do not portray him as frail. Do not portray him as overly emotional. === ENVIRONMENT LOCK === Use the provided village/home reference as the environmental reference. The scene takes place at Riven's family cottage and the familiar training yard beside it. Maintain the recognizable environment: weathered timber-and-stone cottage, rough stone foundation, sloped roof, small chimney, wooden door, nearby chopping block, stacked firewood, simple wooden fence, large old tree, dirt-and-grass training area, and the village road leading out through the valley. The surrounding settlement is a poor but peaceful medieval-fantasy village beneath rugged mountains. The training portion takes place in natural late-afternoon light. The departure takes place the following morning in cool early daylight with light mountain mist. The geography of the cottage, training yard, and road must remain visually consistent. === TECHNICAL === High-end live-action cinematic realistic dark fantasy. 16:9 cinematic widescreen. Feature-film quality. Realistic human anatomy. Natural human movement. Grounded physical interaction. Realistic sword weight and weapon contact. Realistic cloth and hair physics. Maintain strict facial identity, costume consistency, weapon consistency, and body proportions throughout the whole video. Use restrained cinematic camera movement. Keep sword choreography readable. No excessive cuts. No rapid montage. No exaggerated slow motion. No impossible acrobatics. No spinning for spectacle. No supernatural abilities. No magical effects. No glowing weapons. No injury. No blood. All character dialogue in this video must be spoken in natural ENGLISH ONLY. Use clear natural English pronunciation. Every written dialogue line must be spoken verbatim by the specified character. Do not translate the dialogue. No Chinese or Mandarin. No Vietnamese. No Japanese. No Korean. No other spoken language. No additional spoken dialogue. No background intelligible conversations. Accurate visible lip synchronization whenever a character speaks. No narration. No voice-over. No subtitles. No captions. No visible text. No watermark. No logo. Audio should remain grounded: mountain wind, birds, boots against dirt, controlled breathing, realistic sword impacts, quiet morning village ambience, subtle leather and equipment movement. Keep music restrained if present. Do not make the departure melodramatic. === GLOBAL ACTION === Begin with Adult Riven and her father already sparring in the familiar training yard. This is another controlled exchange between two people who have trained together for many years. Riven has become good enough to genuinely challenge him. Her father now increases the pressure. He changes rhythm and forces Riven to react rather than dictate the exchange. Riven defends well. She is not portrayed as inexperienced. Eventually her father uses timing and leverage to disarm her cleanly. Riven's sword falls into the dirt. Neither character is injured. The fight immediately stops. Riven admits that she thought she had beaten him. Her father acknowledges that she did. This is not contradictory: Riven successfully got through his defense earlier, but one successful exchange does not mean she has nothing left to learn. The father already knows that Riven intends to leave. He asks only: "When?" Riven answers: "Tomorrow." No explanation is needed. The father understands. He tells her: "Pick it up." Riven reaches down for her sword. Use that physical movement to transition naturally to the following morning: Riven reaches downward for the sword → visual match transition → Riven reaches downward and lifts her small travel bag. Now she is leaving home. Keep the goodbye restrained. Her father does not give a speech. He does not stop her. Only when Riven begins walking away does he call her name. Then he gives her the lesson that will remain with her: "Remember who you fight for." Riven silently acknowledges him. Then she leaves. === SCENES === Shot 1 — THE LAST EXCHANGE Open directly inside a controlled sword exchange. Riven and her father are already moving. Do not begin with introductions or dialogue. Riven attacks. Her father blocks. Riven changes angle. Her father moves with her. Their swords meet with realistic physical weight. Riven is clearly skilled. She remains balanced through every exchange. She successfully catches one of her father's counters and immediately pressures him. For a moment she appears to have control. Then the father deliberately changes rhythm. Instead of responding immediately to Riven's expected timing, he waits. Riven commits. The father steps off her attack line. He redirects her sword with a compact movement. Riven tries to recover. He uses controlled leverage against her weapon. Riven's sword is knocked cleanly from her hands. The sword lands in the dirt several steps away. CLANG. Everything stops. Father does not point his sword threateningly at Riven. He immediately lowers it. Riven looks toward her fallen sword. She catches her breath. Then looks back at him. Riven says: "I thought I had you." Father answers calmly: "You did." Riven gives him a questioning look. He does not explain. Instead, his attention settles on her for a moment. He knows something else is coming. A quiet pause. Father asks: "When?" Riven understands exactly what he means. She answers: "Tomorrow." Hold briefly. No surprise. No argument. No dramatic reaction. Father already suspected the answer. He glances toward Riven's sword lying in the dirt. Then back at her. Father says: "Pick it up." Shot 2 — THE MATCH Riven looks toward the fallen sword. She walks to it. She bends down. Her hand reaches toward the sword grip. Frame the movement clearly. As Riven's hand closes around the grip— MATCH TRANSITION. Morning. The same physical motion continues visually. Instead of lifting the sword from the dirt, Riven's hand now lifts a small practical travel bag from beside the cottage doorway. The change from afternoon training to cool early morning should immediately communicate that time has passed. No explanatory text. No narration. No dialogue. Riven straightens. Her sword is already secured naturally at her side. She carries only simple travel equipment. She is prepared to leave. Shot 3 — LEAVING HOME Early morning. Light mist hangs over the valley. The village is quiet. Riven steps away from the cottage carrying her travel bag. Her father is already outside. He is not blocking the road. He is not waiting dramatically in front of her. He is simply there. Riven notices him. Father and daughter look at each other. No dialogue. No hug. No crying. No sentimental smile. The silence should feel natural between two people who understand each other extremely well. Riven gives him a small acknowledging nod. Her father returns it. Riven turns toward the village road. She begins walking. Do not have the father follow her. Let several steps pass. Then: Father calls clearly: "Riven." Riven stops. She turns her upper body and looks back at him. The father remains beside the cottage. He looks directly at her. He says: "Remember who you fight for." No other dialogue follows. Hold on Riven. She immediately understands the meaning of the words. Do not make her cry. Do not make her give an emotional speech. Do not have her answer verbally. Riven gives her father one small deliberate nod. Then she turns forward again. Shot 4 — THE ROAD Move behind Riven as she walks down the familiar village road. This is the same road leading outward through the valley. Her pace is steady. She does not hesitate. Her sword moves naturally at her side. Her travel bag rests against her body. The cottage gradually becomes more distant behind her. Briefly return to the father's perspective. He stands beside the home and watches Riven leave. Keep his expression restrained. He does not wave dramatically. He does not call after her again. Return to Riven. As she reaches farther along the road, she briefly slows. She looks back once. From her position, her father and the cottage are now small in the distance. Hold only on the recognition of home. Then Riven turns forward. She continues walking toward the open valley. The camera remains behind her as the road leads toward the mountains and the world beyond the village. CUT. === END STATE FOR CONTINUITY === Adult Riven has left her family home. She carries her own sword and a small amount of travel equipment. Her father remains behind at the family cottage. Their goodbye was restrained. There was no argument. There was no emotional speech. The father's final words to Riven were: "Remember who you fight for." Riven acknowledged him silently. She is now walking away from the village along the road leading through the valley. She has chosen to leave home and pursue the life of a warrior. She has not yet been shown inside the army. She has not yet participated in warfare. End with Riven moving forward toward the wider world. === MOOD === Grounded. Restrained. Purposeful. Bittersweet without becoming sentimental. The first part should feel physical and competitive. The second part should feel quiet and inevitable. The emotional progression is: Father and daughter spar → Father disarms Riven → Riven believes she almost had him → Father acknowledges that she did → "When?" → "Tomorrow." → "Pick it up." → match transition → morning → Riven leaves → Father calls her name → "Remember who you fight for." → Riven silently acknowledges him → she turns away from home → she walks toward the wider world. Do not turn the scene into a long goodbye. Do not add an argument about joining the army. Do not have Father forbid Riven from leaving. Do not have Riven explain her dreams. Do not have either character cry. Do not add another conversation. Let their relationship be communicated through sparring, silence, and a few precise words.
